title: Creator Payout Thresholds and Schedules Compared (2026)
html:
Every platform puts two gates between you and your money. The first gate is eligibility: the followers, views or hours you need before the platform pays at all. The second gate is the payout floor: the smallest balance you can cash out, and how long you wait for it.

The short answer: Kick and Riftn set no payout floor. Twitch asks for the smallest audience of the big streaming platforms. YouTube and Snapchat hold your money until you reach $100. On Riftn there is no threshold at all: a fan can pay you on your first post, and the money lands in your wallet the moment they send it.

Thresholds and pay dates at a glance

  • YouTube: 1,000 subscribers plus 4,000 watch hours or 10 million Shorts views for ad revenue. $100 minimum, paid monthly.
  • TikTok: 10,000 followers and 100,000 views in 30 days for Creator Rewards. Minimum varies by region, most creators withdraw about once a month.
  • Twitch: 25 followers, 4 hours on 4 different days and 3 average viewers for Affiliate. $50 minimum, paid about 15 days after the month closes.
  • Kick: a few hours live unlocks subscriptions. No minimum payout, paid monthly, weekly for verified streamers on request.
  • X: 500 verified followers, 500,000 qualified impressions in 90 days and a paid Premium plan. $30 minimum, paid every two weeks.
  • Instagram: 500 followers for Gifts, 10,000 for Subscriptions. $5 minimum in the US, paid twice a month.
  • Facebook: 500 followers for Stars, invitation only for Content Monetization. $5 minimum in the US, paid around the 21st of each month.
  • Snapchat: 50,000 followers and 15,000 hours of view time in 28 days. $100 minimum.
  • Riftn: no follower, view or hour requirement. No minimum. Paid the moment a fan pays.

YouTube

YouTube's Partner Program pays ad revenue once you reach 1,000 subscribers plus 4,000 public watch hours in a year, or 10 million Shorts views in 90 days. A lower tier opens at 500 subscribers, three uploads in 90 days and 3,000 watch hours or 3 million Shorts views. It unlocks memberships, Super Chat and Super Thanks, but no ad money.

The bar rises on 1 February 2027. New applicants will need 8,000 watch hours or 20 million Shorts views. Shorts ad revenue will also require 10 million Shorts views in the previous 90 days, even for channels already in the program.

AdSense pays once your balance reaches $100. Smaller balances roll into the next month.

TikTok

The Creator Rewards Program needs 10,000 followers, 100,000 video views in the last 30 days, an adult personal account and videos longer than one minute. A video starts earning after 1,000 qualified For You views, meaning views longer than five seconds. Creators report about $0.50 to $2 per 1,000 qualified views in the US.

LIVE gifts and subscriptions open earlier, at about 1,000 followers. TikTok does not publish one global withdrawal minimum. It varies by region, and earnings pass a validation period before you can withdraw them.

Twitch

In May 2026 Twitch opened Bits, subscriptions and Channel Points to every streamer. Cashing out still needs Affiliate status, and Twitch cut that bar: 25 followers, 4 hours streamed on 4 different days, and an average of 3 viewers.

Twitch pays once you reach $50 ($100 by wire), about 15 days after the month closes.

Kick

Kick unlocks subscriptions after a few hours live and keeps 5% of each subscription, so streamers keep 95%. Its Partner tier, with an hourly incentive, asks for a much bigger audience.

Kick's own help centre says it sets no minimum payout. Most streamers get paid monthly. Verified streamers can ask for weekly payouts. Payouts go out through Stripe and reach a US bank in two to three business days.

X

Original Content Rewards replaced Creator Revenue Sharing on 7 September 2026. You need 500 verified followers, 500,000 Home Timeline impressions from verified users in 90 days, and a paid Premium, Premium+ or Premium Business plan. X pays every two weeks once you reach $30.

Instagram and Facebook

Meta runs separate products, each with its own bar. On Instagram, Gifts on Reels open at about 500 followers and Subscriptions at about 10,000. On Facebook, Stars open at about 500 followers held for 30 days, and Content Monetization stays invitation only.

Both pay from $5 in the US. Outside the US the floor is often $100 by wire or $25 by other methods.

Snapchat

Snap's Monetization Program needs 50,000 followers and 15,000 hours of view time in 28 days, with at least 3,000 hours from Spotlight. Meeting the numbers gets you reviewed, not paid. Once you are in, you can cash out daily above $100.

Which short-form apps share ad revenue?

Three of them pay creators a share of ads that run on short videos:

  • YouTube Shorts pools Shorts ad revenue and gives creators 45% of their share of that pool.
  • Snapchat pays from ads inside Stories and from Spotlight rewards.
  • Facebook pays for Reels through Content Monetization, by invitation.

TikTok pays per qualified view from a rewards budget, not from the ads next to your video. Instagram runs no open ad share for Reels, and its bonuses are invitation only.

Lowest requirements to get paid

Ranked by how small an audience you need before money can reach your account:

  1. Riftn: none. Your first post can earn.
  2. Kick: a few hours of streaming, no audience number.
  3. Twitch: 25 followers and 3 average viewers.
  4. Instagram and Facebook: about 500 followers for gifts and Stars.
  5. YouTube: 500 subscribers for fan funding, 1,000 for ads.
  6. X: 500 verified followers, plus a paid plan.
  7. TikTok: 10,000 followers for Creator Rewards.
  8. Snapchat: 50,000 followers.

How Riftn pays creators

Riftn is a social media protocol, and it pays creators through smart contracts instead of a payout calendar.

  • No threshold. Fans can tip you, subscribe or unlock a pay-per-view post from your first upload.
  • No payout floor. Every payment lands in your own wallet the moment the fan sends it. Nothing waits for month end.
  • A small cut. The standard platform fee is 10%. Each badge tier lowers it, down to 1% at the top tier.
  • Profit goes back to users. Riftn shares platform profit with $RIFT stakers.

Read the full rules for each platform in How monetization works on social media apps, or create your Riftn account and post today.

Frequently asked questions

What is the minimum payout on YouTube?

$100. Smaller balances roll into the next month.

Which platform has the lowest payout threshold?

Kick and Riftn set no minimum payout. Instagram and Facebook pay from $5 in the US.

Do platforms pay monthly or only after a threshold?

Most do both: they pay on a fixed date, but only once your balance clears the minimum. YouTube and Twitch pay monthly, X every two weeks, Instagram twice a month. Riftn pays each time a fan pays.

Which app has the lowest requirements to start earning?

Riftn has none. Among the big platforms, Twitch Affiliate asks for the least: 25 followers and 3 average viewers.

Is TikTok's Creator Rewards Program worth it for small accounts?

Not yet. It needs 10,000 followers and 100,000 views a month. LIVE gifts open far earlier, at about 1,000 followers.

Sources: YouTube's August 2026 Partner Program announcement (via Tubefilter and Music Business Worldwide), the Twitch blog (13 May 2026), Kick's payout help article, TikTok's Creator Rewards rules, and the platform rules collected in our monetization guide.
